title: {chip:impinj-m730:name} UHF Inlay — Retail Source Tagging
summary: This Impinj UHF inlay family ({chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} silicon class) is the volume retail workhorse of the M700 family — 96-bit EPC, ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC Gen2v2, factory-serialised TID, no user memory, no AUTHENTICATE. Engineered for the lowest practical silicon ASP at billion-tag scale. Proud Tek supplies {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} inlays in dry / wet / converted-label form for global retail apparel source tagging, footwear, accessories, and high-volume FMCG serialisation programmes that need SGTIN-96 EPC encoding without paying for user memory or chip-level cryptographic features. Retail loss-prevention, source-tagging, and apparel item-level deployments use this as the chip / sensitivity / SGTIN-encoding / Walmart-mandate / converter-ecosystem reference.

brief.label: Chip silicon and lineage
items: {chip:impinj-m730:name} = rebranded {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} silicon under the M700-family naming refresh; datasheets, EPC behaviour, and TID prefix (E280-1160) unchanged.
Existing readers, encoders, and inlays branded as {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} fully interoperable with {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} inlays.
Manufactured at billion-unit scale; the cost-optimised tier of the M700 family below {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name}.

brief.label: Memory architecture
items: 96-bit EPC — sufficient for full SGTIN-96, SSCC-96, GRAI-96, GIAI-96 encoding per GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0.
96-bit serialised factory-programmed TID (E280-1160 prefix) for inventory deduplication, anti-cloning audit trail, and unique-tag identification.
0 bits user memory — cost-optimised; specify {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} if user memory is required for lot / date / encrypted-serial payloads.
32-bit access password + 32-bit kill password per EPC Gen2v2.

brief.label: Sensitivity and read range
items: Read sensitivity: −22.6 dBm typical (datasheet); 0.9 dB below {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} / on par with {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} in retail-floor environments.
Write sensitivity: −16.7 dBm typical — sufficient for printer-encoder throughput at 1,000+ tags / minute.
Free-air bench: 8-10 m on paper hangtag with Impinj R700 at +30 dBm EIRP. Real-world: 6-8 m apparel hangtag, 1.5-2.5 m on-metal with foam spacer, 1.0-2.0 m on-liquid with foam-isolated label.

brief.label: Air interface and standards
items: ISO/IEC 18000-63:2015 + EPC Gen2v2 air interface (basic inventory and read/write commands).
GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard (TDS) 2.0 SGTIN-96 / SSCC-96 / GRAI-96 / GIAI-96 encoding.
Frequency: 860-960 MHz across FCC + ETSI + Japan ARIB + China sub-bands.
RAIN RFID Alliance certified; ARC Master List spec category compliant.

brief.label: Why {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} dominates retail source-tagging
items: Silicon ASP — Impinj sells {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} wafer at the most competitive UHF chip pricing globally because the feature set is intentionally minimal: 96-bit EPC, factory TID, no user memory, no AUTHENTICATE.
Encoder throughput — supports standard EPC Gen2v2 BlockWrite; tolerates high-temperature, high-RF-density retail printer-applicator (Printronix T8000, Zebra ZT411) running at 1,000+ tags / minute.

Inlay ecosystem — every major converter (Avery Dennison / Smartrac, Arizon, HID, Beontag, SML, Trace ID) maintains {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} reference inlays in catalogue antenna designs (AD-227, AD-237, AD-661 and equivalents). New SKU rollouts typically 2-4 weeks ex-stock.

Reader compatibility — fully ISO/IEC 18000-63 + EPC Gen2v2 compliant; every fixed reader (Impinj R700, Zebra FX9600), handheld (Zebra MC3300xR, Impinj IPJ-R0510), and printer-encoder reads/writes {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} with no firmware change.

brief.label: Walmart RFID mandate alignment
items: Walmart RFID source-tag mandate requires SGTIN-96 EPC encoding per GS1 TDS 2.0 — {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} is the volume chip for source-tag compliance across apparel, home, electronics, beauty, hardline.
Adjacent retail mandates: Target, Macy's, Inditex, Nike, Lululemon, Kohl's all run on the same SGTIN encoding stack and accept {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}-class chips.
Walmart accepts ARC Master List spec category certification — Auburn University RFID Lab benchmarks at the procurement reference.

brief.label: Where {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} is NOT the right fit
items: Brand-protection / anti-counterfeiting: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} doesn't implement on-chip crypto. For cryptographic chip-authenticity programmes, mainstream UHF Gen2v2 silicon does NOT implement on-chip AES — specify {chip:impinj-m775:name} (PRESENT-80 on-chip crypto per ISO/IEC 29167-11) or pair the UHF tag with an HF {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} / UCODE DNA companion tag. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} do not have on-chip crypto either.

Pharmaceutical serialisation with on-tag user data: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} has 0 bits user memory. DSCSA / EU FMD encoded data must live in backend database keyed by EPC; for on-tag data choose {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (32-bit user), {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} (688-bit user), or {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} (32-224 bit configurable).

EU Digital Product Passport (DPP): typically requires user memory + chip-level authentication — {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} is insufficient on memory. For URL pointer + user memory, specify {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} or {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}. For per-tap cryptographic authentication, specify M775 or pair with HF {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name}.

Sensor / specialty applications: no sensor variant in {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} line; cold-chain moisture sensing requires {chip:nxp-ucode-9xe:short_name}; tamper detection at UHF requires different specialty silicon.

brief.label: Standard antenna configurations
items: Far-field general-purpose (~70 × 14 mm): retail and supply-chain reference inlay for hangtags, pallet labels, carton labels.
Compact retail (~44 × 14 mm): jewellery, eyewear, accessories, small-item apparel — fits inside 50 × 25 mm hangtag.
On-metal (with foam spacer or specialty antenna): 1.5-2.5 m read on metal; {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} specified instead when on-metal margin is critical.
On-liquid (foam-isolated label, optimised for cosmetics and beverage): 1.0-2.0 m; cost-optimised choice for high-volume FMCG.
Custom antenna designs: 6-10 weeks from spec to first samples; production tooling adds 2-4 weeks.

brief.label: Form factors — dry, wet, converted-label
items: Dry inlay: bare antenna + chip on carrier substrate, no adhesive — for label converters laminating into their own construction.
Wet inlay: pressure-sensitive adhesive on release liner, ready to apply directly.
Converted label: printed face stock + adhesive + inlay = finished branded label ready for end-use application.

brief.label: Encoding and printer-applicator compatibility
items: Printronix T8000-class, Zebra ZT411 / ZE521-class, SATO CL4NX-class printer-encoders write {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} inlays at 1,000+ tags / minute.
BlockWrite + Reserved-area programming for SGTIN-96 + access password + kill password in single pass.
Compatible with retail-grade encoder workflows from FineLine Technologies, Avery Dennison Janela, SML EcoTech, ChainPoint.

brief.label: Procurement and lead times
items: MOQ 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs (general-purpose far-field, compact retail, on-metal, on-liquid, windshield).
Custom antenna designs: MOQ 50,000-100,000 pieces depending on tooling depth.
Sample sets of 100-500 pieces available for evaluation; lead time 3-4 weeks for stock antenna, 6-10 weeks for new antenna tooling.

sections.title: What {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} is NOT the right fit for

dataHighlight.heading: User memory on {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} — by design
dataHighlight.text: The {chip:impinj-m730:short_name}'s defining cost-optimisation is the absence of user memory. Programmes that need on-tag data — pharmaceutical serialisation with batch / expiration on the tag, EU Digital Product Passport URL pointer, on-tag encrypted serial — must specify a different chip. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} ({chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:short_name}) adds 32-bit user memory + Protected Mode (Gen2v2 Untraceable) at ~30% silicon-ASP premium. {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} offers 32-224-bit configurable user memory. {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} offers 688-bit user memory (the largest in commodity UHF). For per-tap cryptographic authentication (the AUTHENTICATE silicon implementation, AES on-chip), no mainstream M700-family chip qualifies except M775 (PRESENT-80 per ISO/IEC 29167-11) — pair UHF inventory tags with HF {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} on per-tap-crypto programmes. The chip-family decision is not about read range (all are within ~1 dB sensitivity of each other) — it's about whether the programme needs user memory and what privacy / crypto features it requires.
dataHighlight.source: {chip:impinj-m730:name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / M775 product briefs + GS1 TDS 2.0 + RAIN Alliance retail source-tagging guidance

bullets: On-chip cryptographic chip authentication: choose M775 (PRESENT-80) or pair UHF with HF {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} / UCODE DNA — {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:impinj-m770:short_name} do NOT carry on-chip crypto.
Pharmaceutical with on-tag batch / expiry: choose {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (32-bit user) or {chip:alien-higgs-9:short_name} (688-bit user) — {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} has 0 bits user memory.

EU Digital Product Passport: choose {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} or {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} — DPP needs URL pointer + user memory. For per-tap crypto verification add HF {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name}.
Sensor applications: choose {chip:nxp-ucode-9xe:short_name} — no sensor variant in {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} line.

sections.title: Inside the M730 inlay — dipole, strap, and a die stripped for cost
sections.intro: A UHF inlay is deliberately unglamorous hardware: a stamped metal dipole, a die about the size of a coarse grain of sand flip-chipped onto a strap, and a substrate to hold the two flat. Almost none of the unit cost hides in the antenna — it hides in that speck of silicon, which is why choosing between chip families is a memory-and-sensitivity argument rather than an antenna one; walk the [full UHF chip comparison](/compare/ucode8-vs-ucode9-vs-monza-r6-vs-higgs9/) before you commit a programme. The same M730 inlay then ships in three finishes depending on who laminates the label, and [the rest of the RFID label range](/products/rfid-labels/) covers the housings built around it.

image.alt: Flat anatomy of an M730 UHF RAIN inlay: a stamped copper or aluminium dipole antenna tuned 860-960 MHz on a PET or paper substrate, a flip-chip strap carrying the M730 (Monza R6) die at the centre, and the three delivery forms — dry inlay, wet inlay, and converted label.

bullets: Dipole antenna: stamped or etched copper / aluminium, tuned across the 860-960 MHz UHF band — this, not the chip, is what sets read range.
Flip-chip strap: the M730 (Monza R6-class) die is bonded to a small strap first, which is what lets a single die drop into dozens of catalogue antenna designs without re-bonding.
Substrate: a PET or paper carrier the antenna is printed onto — paper for disposable retail hangtags, PET film where the label has to survive handling.

Two stock antenna families cover most retail: far-field general-purpose (~70 × 14 mm) for hangtags, cartons and pallet labels, and compact retail (~44 × 14 mm) for jewellery, eyewear and small-item apparel.

sections.title: How far an M730 reads — set by the surface, not the silicon
sections.intro: The most common buyer question is read range, and the honest answer points at the mounting surface, not the datasheet. The M730 die never changes, yet a paper hangtag in free air behaves nothing like the same inlay foam-spaced off a steel shelf edge or floated over a bottle of shampoo. The ranges below are what you can plan against per surface, measured on an Impinj R700 at +30 dBm EIRP — the same numbers behind the [retail apparel and Walmart source-tag](/industries/retail-apparel/) deployments. If a programme needs on-tag user memory or a harder on-metal margin, that is the cue to [step up to the M750](/products/rfid-labels/impinj-m750-uhf-inlay/).

image.alt: Horizontal bar chart of M730 read range by mounting surface, measured on an Impinj R700 at +30 dBm EIRP: free-air paper hangtag 8-10 m, apparel hangtag 6-8 m, on-metal with a foam spacer 1.5-2.5 m, and on-liquid with a foam-isolated label 1.0-2.0 m, with a note that pallet and carton portals read 98-99% on dense loads.

rows: Margin is tight; pilot before rollout, or M750
Cost-optimised FMCG; validate per bottle geometry

bullets: Read range is an antenna-and-surface property, not a chip spec: the same M730 die spans 8-10 m in free air and 1.0-2.0 m over liquid.
Pallet and carton dock-door portals are graded on read rate, not distance — 98-99% on dense mixed loads is the retail throughput target.
On metal and on liquid both detune the antenna; a foam spacer or a dedicated on-metal antenna design buys back the 1.5-2.5 m and 1.0-2.0 m figures in the table above.
Always confirm with an on-site pilot before committing volume: reader power, antenna gain, tag orientation and the tagged product itself all move these numbers.

faq.question: What is the difference between {chip:impinj-m730:name} and {chip:impinj-m750:short_name}?
faq.answer: {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} (Monza R6 class) is the cost-optimised variant: 96-bit EPC, no user memory, no EPC Gen2v2 AUTHENTICATE or Untraceable. {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} (Monza R6-P class) adds {chip:impinj-m750:user_bits} bits of user memory + full AUTHENTICATE and Untraceable + Hide-EPC at ~30% silicon-ASP premium. Choose {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} for pure SGTIN-96 retail volume; choose {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} for brand authentication, retail-privacy at POS, on-tag user memory, or any cryptographic verification requirement.

faq.question: Is {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} the same chip as {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name}?
faq.answer: Yes — Impinj rebranded {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} silicon as {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} under the M700-series naming refresh. Datasheets, EPC behaviour, and TID prefix (E280-1160) unchanged. Existing readers, encoders, and inlays branded as {chip:impinj-monza-r6:short_name} fully interoperable with {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} inlays.

faq.question: What read range can I expect from a Proud Tek {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} inlay?
faq.answer: Free-air on a paper hangtag with Impinj R700 reader at +30 dBm EIRP: 8-10 m. Apparel hangtags: 6-8 m. On metal with foam-spaced specialty antenna: 1.5-2.5 m. On liquid (cosmetics / beverage) with foam-isolated label: 1.0-2.0 m. Pallet portal read rates: 98-99% on dense loads. Real numbers depend on antenna design, reader power, and deployment substrate. Always validate with on-site pilot before committing.

faq.question: Can {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} be used with my existing Impinj R700 / Zebra FX9600 reader fleet?
faq.answer: Yes — fully ISO/IEC 18000-63 + EPC Gen2v2 compliant. Every standards-compliant fixed reader, handheld, and printer-encoder reads/writes {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} with no firmware change. The advanced EPC Gen2v2 commands (Untraceable, AUTHENTICATE, Hide-EPC) that {chip:impinj-m750:short_name} / {chip:nxp-ucode-9:short_name} implement are not available on {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} — but basic inventory and read/write commands work identically.

faq.question: What MOQ does Proud Tek offer for {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} inlays?
faq.answer: 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs (general-purpose far-field, compact retail, on-metal, on-liquid, windshield). For custom antenna designs MOQ is typically 50,000-100,000 pieces depending on tooling depth. Sample sets of 100-500 pieces available for evaluation; lead time 3-4 weeks for stock antenna designs, 6-10 weeks for new antenna tooling.

faq.question: Does {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} meet the Walmart RFID mandate?
faq.answer: Yes — the dominant chip behind Walmart RFID source-tagging compliance. Walmart requires SGTIN-96 EPC encoding per GS1 TDS 2.0 with ARC Master List spec category certification on the inlay design. {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} + ARC-certified antenna meets both requirements. Walmart's mandate has expanded from apparel (2020) to home / electronics / beauty / hardline (2022-2024); {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} ships into all categories. Adjacent mandates (Target, Macy's, Inditex, Nike, Lululemon, Kohl's) accept the same {chip:impinj-m730:short_name} + ARC-certified-antenna stack.
